claim: The P2X7 receptor is a non-selective cation channel activated by extracellular adenosine triphosphate (ATP).
source: The P2X7 receptor is a non-selective cation channel activated by extracellular adenosine triphosphate (ATP).
evidence: This is a definitional statement about P2X7 receptor function that is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Chronic activation of P2X7 underlies many health problems such as pathologic pain.
source: Chronic activation of P2X7 underlies many health problems such as pathologic pain, yet we lack effective antagonists due to poorly understood mechanisms of inhibition.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge about P2X7's role in disease.

claim: We lack effective antagonists for P2X7 due to poorly understood mechanisms of inhibition.
source: Chronic activation of P2X7 underlies many health problems such as pathologic pain, yet we lack effective antagonists due to poorly understood mechanisms of inhibition.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of drug development and mechanistic understanding.

claim: Five structurally-unrelated antagonists all bind to an allosteric site distinct from the ATP-binding pocket in a groove formed between two neighboring subunits.
source: Unexpectedly, these drugs all bind to an allosteric site distinct from the ATP-binding pocket in a groove formed between two neighboring subunits.
evidence: This claim is supported by crystal structures showing drug binding locations.

claim: The novel drug-binding pocket accommodates a diversity of small molecules mainly through hydrophobic interactions.
source: This novel drug-binding pocket accommodates a diversity of small molecules mainly through hydrophobic interactions.
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis of the drug-binding pocket and the chemical nature of the interactions.

claim: The antagonists allosterically prevent narrowing of the drug-binding pocket and the turret-like architecture during channel opening.
source: Functional assays propose that these compounds allosterically prevent narrowing of the drug-binding pocket and the turret-like architecture during channel opening, which is consistent with a site of action distal to the ATP-binding pocket.
evidence: This is supported by functional assays including cysteine accessibility experiments.

claim: Chronic pain debilitates more than 10% of adults globally.
source: Chronic pain is a major public health epidemic, debilitating more than 10% of adults globally with afflictions like persisting headaches, lower back pain, and rheumatoid arthritis (Gold and Gebhart, 2010; Goldberg and McGee, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Gold and Gebhart, 2010 and Goldberg and McGee, 2011.

claim: Many chronic pain patients are resistant to commonly used analgesics.
source: While some patients are responsive to commonly used analgesics, many are resistant to treatment (Dworkin et al., 2007; Finnerup et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Dworkin et al., 2007 and Finnerup et al., 2010.

claim: The P2X7 receptor is predominantly expressed in immune cells of the blood and the brain.
source: The P2X7 receptor, an extracellular ATP-gated ion channel predominantly expressed in immune cells of the blood and the brain (Surprenant et al., 1996; Habermacher et al., 2016), is an emerging target for treating refractory pain (Chessell et al., 2005; Gum et al., 2012; Burnstock, 2013; North and Jarvis, 2013; Sperlágh and Illes, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Surprenant et al., 1996 and Habermacher et al., 2016.

claim: The P2X7 receptor is an emerging target for treating refractory pain.
source: The P2X7 receptor, an extracellular ATP-gated ion channel predominantly expressed in immune cells of the blood and the brain (Surprenant et al., 1996; Habermacher et al., 2016), is an emerging target for treating refractory pain (Chessell et al., 2005; Gum et al., 2012; Burnstock, 2013; North and Jarvis, 2013; Sperlágh and Illes, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations: Chessell et al., 2005; Gum et al., 2012; Burnstock, 2013; North and Jarvis, 2013; Sperlágh and Illes, 2014.

claim: P2X7 specific antagonists have been demonstrated to alleviate chronic pain in animal models.
source: Over the last decade, enormous effort has been made to develop a number of structurally distinct P2X7 specific antagonists, some of which have been demonstrated to alleviate chronic pain in animal models (Honore et al., 2006a; McGaraughty et al., 2007; Bartlett et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Honore et al., 2006a; McGaraughty et al., 2007; Bartlett et al., 2014.

claim: Mechanisms of action for P2X7 antagonists remain poorly understood.
source: However, mechanisms of action for these drugs remain poorly understood, hampering the development of effective therapeutic compounds for human patients (Keystone et al., 2012; Stock et al., 2012; Bhattacharya and Biber, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Keystone et al., 2012; Stock et al., 2012; Bhattacharya and Biber, 2016.

claim: P2X receptors are trimeric ligand-gated ion channels.
source: P2X receptors are trimeric ligand-gated ion channels that facilitate extracellular-ATP mediated signaling along with the G protein-coupled P2Y receptors (North, 2002; Burnstock, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to North, 2002 and Burnstock, 2014.

claim: The P2X7 receptor was originally identified as 'the P2Z receptor'.
source: The P2X7 receptor belongs to the P2X receptor family, however, it was originally identified as a unique ATP-receptor named "the P2Z receptor", as it harbors many characteristics distinct from P2X and P2Y receptors (Di Virgilio, 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Di Virgilio, 1995.

claim: The P2X7 receptor requires an unusually high concentration of ATP (EC50 ≥ 1 mM under physiological ion concentrations) for initial activation.
source: For instance, the P2X7 receptor requires an unusually high concentration of ATP (EC50 ≥ 1 mM under physiological ion concentrations) for initial activation (Yan et al., 2010), its channel activity is facilitated by prolonged or repeated ATP applications (Surprenant et al., 1996), and it opens a membrane pore large enough for molecules up to ~900 Da to permeate (Steinberg et al., 1987; Nuttle and Dubyak, 1994; Yan et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Yan et al., 2010.

claim: P2X7 channel activity is facilitated by prolonged or repeated ATP applications.
source: For instance, the P2X7 receptor requires an unusually high concentration of ATP (EC50 ≥ 1 mM under physiological ion concentrations) for initial activation (Yan et al., 2010), its channel activity is facilitated by prolonged or repeated ATP applications (Surprenant et al., 1996), and it opens a membrane pore large enough for molecules up to ~900 Da to permeate (Steinberg et al., 1987; Nuttle and Dubyak, 1994; Yan et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Surprenant et al., 1996.

claim: The P2X7 receptor opens a membrane pore large enough for molecules up to ~900 Da to permeate.
source: For instance, the P2X7 receptor requires an unusually high concentration of ATP (EC50 ≥ 1 mM under physiological ion concentrations) for initial activation (Yan et al., 2010), its channel activity is facilitated by prolonged or repeated ATP applications (Surprenant et al., 1996), and it opens a membrane pore large enough for molecules up to ~900 Da to permeate (Steinberg et al., 1987; Nuttle and Dubyak, 1994; Yan et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Steinberg et al., 1987; Nuttle and Dubyak, 1994; Yan et al., 2008.

claim: Crystal structures of the P2X3 and P2X4 receptors have uncovered common mechanisms such as ATP-binding and gating for the P2X receptor family.
source: While crystal structures of the P2X3 and P2X4 receptors have uncovered common mechanisms such as ATP-binding and gating for the P2X receptor family (Kawate et al., 2009; Hattori and Gouaux, 2012; Mansoor et al., 2016), many questions continue to exist regarding subtype specific mechanisms, especially for the enigmatic P2X7 receptor subtype.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kawate et al., 2009; Hattori and Gouaux, 2012; Mansoor et al., 2016.

claim: The truncated pdP2X7 expressed better than other orthologues in insect cells.
source: Using fluorescence detection size exclusion chromatography (FSEC) (Kawate and Gouaux, 2006), we screened full-length and a series of C-terminally truncated versions of nine human P2X7 (hP2X7) orthologues (72–89% identical), and found that an artificially truncated version of the panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca) P2X7 receptor (pdP2X7) not only expressed better than other orthologues in insect cells but also remained trimeric and monodisperse in detergents commonly used for crystallography (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by FSEC screening data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The truncated pdP2X7 remained trimeric and monodisperse in detergents commonly used for crystallography.
source: Using fluorescence detection size exclusion chromatography (FSEC) (Kawate and Gouaux, 2006), we screened full-length and a series of C-terminally truncated versions of nine human P2X7 (hP2X7) orthologues (72–89% identical), and found that an artificially truncated version of the panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca) P2X7 receptor (pdP2X7) not only expressed better than other orthologues in insect cells but also remained trimeric and monodisperse in detergents commonly used for crystallography (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by FSEC data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: pdP2X7 presents comparable characteristics to hP2X7.
source: Whole cell patch clamp recordings confirmed that pdP2X7 presents comparable characteristics to hP2X7 (Figure 1B–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by whole cell patch clamp recordings shown in Figure 1B-G.

claim: pdP2X7cryst exhibited slower deactivation compared to wildtype pdP2X7.
source: pdP2X7cryst exhibited slower deactivation and no obvious current facilitation (run-up) after repeated ATP applications (Figure 1C and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 1C and F.

claim: pdP2X7cryst exhibited no obvious current facilitation (run-up) after repeated ATP applications.
source: pdP2X7cryst exhibited slower deactivation and no obvious current facilitation (run-up) after repeated ATP applications (Figure 1C and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 1C and F.

claim: A single subunit of the P2X7 receptor resembles the 'dolphin-like' shape of zebrafish P2X4 and human P2X3.
source: Overall, a single subunit of the P2X7 receptor resembles the 'dolphin-like' shape of zebrafish P2X4 (zfP2X4; 45% identical to pdP2X7) (Kawate et al., 2009; Hattori and Gouaux, 2012) and human P2X3 (hP2X3; 38% identical to pdP2X7) (Mansoor et al., 2016), the other P2X receptor subtypes with known architecture (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, and citations to previous structures.

claim: The P2X7 structure obtained in the absence of antagonists (apo-form) likely represents a closed conformation.
source: The P2X7 structure obtained in the absence of antagonists (apo-form) likely represents a closed conformation, as the transmembrane helices constrict the channel gate at residues G338, S339, and S342 (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis of the transmembrane helices shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The transmembrane helices constrict the channel gate at residues G338, S339, and S342 in the apo-form.
source: The P2X7 structure obtained in the absence of antagonists (apo-form) likely represents a closed conformation, as the transmembrane helices constrict the channel gate at residues G338, S339, and S342 (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The structural resemblance of the transmembrane helices between P2X7 and zfP2X4 in the closed state (RMSD of the protomers is 2.8 Å) supports that the apo-structure represents a closed conformation.
source: The structural resemblance of the transmembrane helices between our current P2X7 and the zfP2X4 in the closed state (root-mean-square displacement (RMSD) of the protomers is 2.8 Å) also supports that our apo-structure represents a closed conformation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RMSD calculation and structural comparison shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Antagonist-bound P2X7 structures represent the same closed conformation with a RMSD of less than 0.5 Å to the apo structure.
source: Likewise, antagonist-bound P2X7 structures represent the same closed conformation with a RMSD of less than 0.5 Å to the apo structure, indicating that these drugs likely stabilize a resting closed state.
evidence: This claim is supported by RMSD calculations comparing antagonist-bound and apo structures.

claim: The antagonists likely stabilize a resting closed state.
source: Likewise, antagonist-bound P2X7 structures represent the same closed conformation with a RMSD of less than 0.5 Å to the apo structure, indicating that these drugs likely stabilize a resting closed state.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the structural similarity between antagonist-bound and apo structures.

claim: All five structurally-unrelated compounds bind in the same pocket formed between neighboring subunits.
source: Surprisingly, all five structurally-unrelated compounds bind in the same pocket formed between neighboring subunits, which is juxtaposed with the ATP-binding pocket (Figure 2C–D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by crystal structures showing drug binding locations in Figure 2C-D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The drug-binding pocket is juxtaposed with the ATP-binding pocket.
source: Surprisingly, all five structurally-unrelated compounds bind in the same pocket formed between neighboring subunits, which is juxtaposed with the ATP-binding pocket (Figure 2C–D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 2C-D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The drug-binding pocket is surrounded by thirteen residues projecting mainly from β-strands (β4, β13 and β14) in the upper body domains of the neighboring subunits.
source: This drug-binding pocket is surrounded by thirteen residues projecting mainly from β-strands (β4, β13 and β14) in the upper body domains of the neighboring subunits (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Drug binding seems to be mediated mainly by hydrophobic interactions, especially at positions deep within the cavity, involving F95, F103, M105, F293, and V312.
source: Drug binding seems to be mediated mainly by hydrophobic interactions, especially at positions deep within the cavity, involving F95, F103, M105, F293, and V312.
evidence: This claim is based on structural analysis of the drug-binding pocket and the chemical nature of the residues.

claim: The equivalent pocket in the P2X4 receptor is too narrow to accommodate the smallest P2X7 antagonist, A804598.
source: Indeed, the equivalent pocket in the P2X4 receptor is too narrow to accommodate the smallest P2X7 antagonist, A804598, even though it is similarly hydrophobic to that of the P2X7 receptor (Figure 3—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 3—figure supplements 2 and 3.

claim: The differences in the size of the inter-subunit hydrophobic pocket is the major factor that confers P2X7 specific binding of the inhibitors.
source: Thus, we suggest that the differences in the size of the inter-subunit hydrophobic pocket is the major factor that confers P2X7 specific binding of the inhibitors.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the structural comparison between P2X7 and P2X4 drug-binding pockets.

claim: Alanine mutants F103C, K110C, T308C, and I310C showed irreversible current reduction when MTS-TPAE was applied in the absence of ATP.
source: When MTS-TPAE was applied in the absence of ATP, four cysteine mutants (F103C, K110C, T308C, and I310C) showed irreversible current reduction (Figure 4E and F), consistent with the idea that the covalently bound MTS-TPAE at these positions hinders the conformational changes required for channel opening.
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 4E and F.

claim: None of the cysteine mutants presented significant current reduction when MTS-TPAE was applied in the presence of ATP.
source: When MTS-TPAE was applied in the presence of ATP, on the other hand, none of the cysteine mutants presented significant current reduction (Figure 4E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 4E and F.

claim: At least four residues in the drug-binding pocket are more accessible to MTS-TPAE in the closed state than in the open state.
source: These results indicate that at least four residues in the drug-binding pocket are more accessible to MTS-TPAE in the closed state than in the open state.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the differential accessibility of cysteine mutants to MTS-TPAE in closed vs. open states.

claim: The drug-binding pocket narrows upon ATP binding.
source: Our data therefore suggest that the drug-binding pocket narrows upon ATP binding and that such a conformational rearrangement is crucial for P2X7 channel opening.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the cysteine accessibility experiments showing reduced accessibility in the open state.

claim: Narrowing of the drug-binding pocket is crucial for P2X7 channel opening.
source: Our data therefore suggest that the drug-binding pocket narrows upon ATP binding and that such a conformational rearrangement is crucial for P2X7 channel opening.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the cysteine accessibility experiments and the effect of MTS-TPAE modification on channel activity.

claim: MTS-TPAE diminished the Y295C channel activity by ~80% in the absence of ATP but to a lesser extent (~40%) in the presence of ATP.
source: Under these conditions, MTS-TPAE diminished the Y295C channel activity by ~80% in the absence of ATP but to a lesser extent (~40%) in the presence of ATP (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 5B and C.

claim: The turret narrows during P2X7 activation.
source: These data support that the turret also narrows during P2X7 activation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the differential accessibility of Y295C to MTS-TPAE in closed vs. open states.

claim: Narrowing of the inter-subunit space seems unique to the P2X7 receptor.
source: Notably, narrowing of the inter-subunit space seems unique to the P2X7 receptor, as suggested by the crystal structures of P2X3 and P2X4 solved in the presence of ATP.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison with P2X3 and P2X4 crystal structures and functional data.

claim: MTS-TPAE application either in the presence or absence of ATP did not exhibit current reduction for cysteine mutants of the counterpart residues in the P2X4 receptor.
source: Indeed, MTS-TPAE application either in the presence or absence of ATP did not exhibit current reduction for cysteine mutants of the counterpart residues in the P2X4 receptor (Figure 5B and E, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 5B and E, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: ATP-binding brings the dorsal fin domain towards the head domain and pushes the left flipper domain away from the ATP-binding pocket.
source: Consistent with the activation mechanisms proposed for P2X3 and P2X4, ATP-binding brings the dorsal fin domain towards the head domain and pushes the left flipper domain away from the ATP-binding pocket (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 6C.

claim: ATP-binding movements are coupled with widening of the lower body domain.
source: These movements are coupled with widening of the lower body domain (Figure 6D), though to an extent in which the transmembrane helices remain closed.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Little conformational change was observed for the upper body domain including the turret and the drug-binding pockets in the ATP/A804598-bound structure.
source: In contrast, little conformational change was observed for the upper body domain including the turret and the drug-binding pockets (Figure 6A), supporting that the turret closure is essential for P2X7 channel opening.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Turret closure is essential for P2X7 channel opening.
source: In contrast, little conformational change was observed for the upper body domain including the turret and the drug-binding pockets (Figure 6A), supporting that the turret closure is essential for P2X7 channel opening.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the structural observation that the turret does not close when A804598 is bound along with ATP.

claim: P2X7 receptors undergo unique conformational rearrangements where both the drug-binding pocket and the turret narrow upon ATP-binding.
source: Altogether, our data suggest that P2X7 receptors undergo unique conformational rearrangements where both the drug-binding pocket and the turret in the P2X7 receptor narrow upon ATP-binding.
evidence: This claim is supported by cysteine accessibility experiments and structural analysis.

claim: Binding of the P2X7 antagonists preclude the constrictions of the drug-binding pocket and turret, thereby efficiently blocking receptor activation.
source: Because such conformational changes are required for channel opening, binding of the P2X7 antagonists preclude these constrictions, thereby efficiently blocking receptor activation (Figure 7 and Video 2).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the structural and functional data showing that antagonists prevent conformational changes.

claim: The turrets of both P2X3 and P2X4 are narrower even in the closed state compared to P2X7.
source: Interestingly, the turrets of both P2X3 and P2X4 are narrower even in the closed state, which may facilitate subsequent conformational changes in the lower body domain.
evidence: This claim is based on structural comparison between P2X7, P2X3, and P2X4.

claim: The narrower turrets in P2X3 and P2X4 may facilitate subsequent conformational changes in the lower body domain.
source: Interestingly, the turrets of both P2X3 and P2X4 are narrower even in the closed state, which may facilitate subsequent conformational changes in the lower body domain.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on structural observations.

claim: ATP-bound P2X7 receptors are prone to aggregation in a detergent containing solution.
source: However, it is technically challenging to obtain such a crystal structure, as ATP-bound P2X7 receptors are prone to aggregation in a detergent containing solution.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental observations during crystallization attempts.

claim: All five tested drugs are allosteric and non-competitive inhibitors.
source: Our data demonstrate that all five tested drugs are allosteric and non-competitive inhibitors, which is in contrast to the previous studies showing that A740003, A804598, and JNJ47965567 are competitive inhibitors (Honore et al., 2006b; Donnelly-Roberts et al., 2009; Bhattacharya et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by functional assays including dose-response curves, Schild plots, and ATP-binding assays.

claim: Previous studies showed that A740003, A804598, and JNJ47965567 are competitive inhibitors.
source: Our data demonstrate that all five tested drugs are allosteric and non-competitive inhibitors, which is in contrast to the previous studies showing that A740003, A804598, and JNJ47965567 are competitive inhibitors (Honore et al., 2006b; Donnelly-Roberts et al., 2009; Bhattacharya et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Honore et al., 2006b; Donnelly-Roberts et al., 2009; Bhattacharya et al., 2013.

claim: The discrepancy between current and previous studies may be attributed to the high agonist concentrations required for obtaining reliable EC50 values in the presence of antagonists.
source: This discrepancy may be attributed to the high agonist concentrations (i.e. up to 3 mM ATP or 1 mM BzATP) required for obtaining reliable EC50 values in the presence of antagonists.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the discrepancy with previous studies.

claim: The Schild plots of A740003, A804598, and JNJ47965567 appear to be linear at lower concentrations.
source: Nevertheless, the Schild plots of these three compounds appear to be linear at lower concentrations (Figure 3D), making it difficult to rely solely on the Schild regression analysis for determining the mode of drug action.
evidence: This claim is supported by the Schild plot data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Replacing the phenyl group in JNJ47965567 with a slightly bulkier group may increase the binding affinity of this compound.
source: For example, replacing the phenyl group in JNJ47965567 with a slightly bulkier group may increase the binding affinity of this compound, as that would fill the void around residue F95.
evidence: This is a speculative suggestion based on structural analysis of the drug-binding pocket.

claim: Low potency of AZ10606120 and GW791343 may be overcome by replacing chemical moieties with those fit better into the drug-binding pocket.
source: Likewise, low potency of AZ10606120 and GW791343 (Table 1) may be overcome by replacing chemical moieties with those fit better into the drug-binding pocket.
evidence: This is a speculative suggestion based on structural analysis and potency data.

claim: It may be possible to attach an extra chemical group to the site away from the residue interacting with F103 without affecting binding of the P2X7 antagonists.
source: Our data also suggest that it may be possible to attach an extra chemical group to the site away from the residue interacting with F103 without affecting binding of the P2X7 antagonists.
evidence: This is a speculative suggestion based on structural analysis of drug-receptor interactions.

claim: These drugs could be conjugated with cell penetrating peptides or specific ligands expressed on endothelial cells, which may improve the delivery of drugs across the blood-brain barrier.
source: This leads to an interesting possibility that these drugs could be conjugated with cell penetrating peptides or specific ligands expressed on endothelial cells, which may improve the delivery of drugs across the blood-brain barrier (Chen and Liu, 2012).
evidence: This is a speculative suggestion with a citation to Chen and Liu, 2012.

claim: Development of a new generation of P2X7 antagonists with increased clinical efficacy has the potential to have a significant impact on the treatment of chronic pain and inflammation.
source: Development of a new generation of P2X7 antagonists with increased clinical efficacy has the potential to have a significant impact on the treatment of chronic pain and inflammation.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential impact of future drug development.

claim: The EC50 value of pdP2X7 is 122 μM.
source: EC50 values of pdP2X7 and pdP2X7cryst were 122 μM and 40 μM, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by dose-response data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The EC50 value of pdP2X7cryst is 40 μM.
source: EC50 values of pdP2X7 and pdP2X7cryst were 122 μM and 40 μM, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by dose-response data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Mutants F88A, F95A, F103A, M105A, F108A, and V312A showed increased IC50 values.
source: Consistent with the crystal structures, the mutants, F88A, F95A, F103A, M105A, F108A, and V312A, showed increased IC50 values (see Table 1 for IC50 values on the wildtype), supporting that these residues play important roles in drug binding (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by mutagenesis data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 4B.

claim: Interaction with F103 is crucial for the inhibitory action of all five drugs.
source: In particular, interaction with F103 is crucial for the inhibitory action of all five drugs.
evidence: This claim is supported by mutagenesis data showing that F103A mutation affects all five drugs.

claim: Previous studies using cell-based Ca2+ influx and IL-1β release assays proposed that A740003, A804598, and JNJ47965567 compete against ATP-binding to inhibit the P2X7 receptor.
source: However, previous studies using cell-based Ca2+ influx and IL-1β release assays proposed that three of those compounds, A740003, A804598, and JNJ47965567, compete against ATP-binding to inhibit the P2X7 receptor (Honore et al., 2006a; Donnelly-Roberts et al., 2009; Bhattacharya et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Honore et al., 2006a; Donnelly-Roberts et al., 2009; Bhattacharya et al., 2013.

claim: Dose response curves fit well with a non-competitive inhibition model for each drug.
source: For each drug, dose response curves fit well with a non-competitive inhibition model (Kenakin, 2006), but poorly with a competitive model (Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by curve fitting analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 5.

claim: Dose response curves fit poorly with a competitive inhibition model for each drug.
source: For each drug, dose response curves fit well with a non-competitive inhibition model (Kenakin, 2006), but poorly with a competitive model (Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by curve fitting analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 5.

claim: The Schild plots displayed non-linear relationships, especially at higher concentrations, consistent with a non-competitive mechanism.
source: Furthermore, the Schild plots displayed non-linear relationships, especially at higher concentrations, consistent with a non-competitive mechanism (Figure 3D) (Schild, 1947).
evidence: This claim is supported by Schild plot analysis shown in Figure 3D and citation to Schild, 1947.

claim: Alexa-ATP is as potent as ATP and is capable of triggering P2X7 channel opening at 10 μM in the absence of divalent cations.
source: We exploited fluorescence anisotropy (Figure 3—figure supplement 6A–C) using a fluorescently-labeled ATP analogue (Alexa-ATP), which is as potent as ATP and is capable of triggering P2X7 channel opening at 10 μM in the absence of divalent cations (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Alexa-ATP gave rise to fluorescence anisotropy when incubated with P2X7 in a dose-dependent manner.
source: At this concentration, Alexa-ATP gave rise to fluorescence anisotropy when incubated with P2X7 in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 3—figure supplement 6D).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence anisotropy data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 6D.

claim: Drug-treated P2X7 receptor exhibited similar levels of fluorescence anisotropy to untreated receptor.
source: Notably, drug-treated P2X7 receptor exhibited similar levels of fluorescence anisotropy, which drastically decreased in the presence of unlabeled-ATP (Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 6E).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence anisotropy data shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 6E.

claim: Fluorescence anisotropy of drug-treated P2X7 drastically decreased in the presence of unlabeled-ATP.
source: Notably, drug-treated P2X7 receptor exhibited similar levels of fluorescence anisotropy, which drastically decreased in the presence of unlabeled-ATP (Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 6E).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence anisotropy data shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 6E.

claim: The five studied drugs antagonize the P2X7 receptor through a common mechanism.
source: We propose that the five studied drugs antagonize the P2X7 receptor through a common mechanism and that the unique inter-subunit cavity may be a critical locus for functional regulation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the structural and functional data showing all five drugs bind to the same site and act non-competitively.

claim: The unique inter-subunit cavity may be a critical locus for functional regulation.
source: We propose that the five studied drugs antagonize the P2X7 receptor through a common mechanism and that the unique inter-subunit cavity may be a critical locus for functional regulation.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the structural and functional data.

claim: The inter-subunit cavity formed by β13 and β14 in the upper body domain is much wider in P2X7 than in zfP2X4 or in hP2X3.
source: Interestingly, the inter-subunit cavity formed by β13 and β14 in the upper body domain is much wider in P2X7 than in zfP2X4 or in hP2X3 (Figure 4A–C) (Mansoor et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 4A-C and citation to Mansoor et al., 2016.

claim: The turret-like structure and the cleft corresponding to the P2X7 drug-binding pocket remain relatively occluded in zfP2X4 and in hP2X3 after activation by ATP.
source: Furthermore, this 'turret-like' structure and the cleft corresponding to the P2X7 drug-binding pocket remain relatively occluded in zfP2X4 and in hP2X3 after activation by ATP (Figure 4A–C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1) (Mansoor et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 4A-C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1, and citation to Mansoor et al., 2016.

claim: Closure of the turret is a prerequisite for full-widening of the lower body domain, which is necessary for channel opening.
source: Closure of the turret, therefore, seems to be a prerequisite for full-widening of the lower body domain, which is necessary for channel opening.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the structural and functional data showing that preventing turret closure blocks channel opening.

claim: The ATP-binding left flipper domain is connected with the pore-lining transmembrane helix through the turret composed of two β-strands (β13 and β14).
source: Indeed, the ATP-binding left flipper domain is connected with the pore-lining transmembrane helix through the turret composed of two β-strands (β13 and β14), which supports that movements of the upper body domain are tightly coupled with the channel opening (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Movements of the upper body domain are tightly coupled with the channel opening.
source: Indeed, the ATP-binding left flipper domain is connected with the pore-lining transmembrane helix through the turret composed of two β-strands (β13 and β14), which supports that movements of the upper body domain are tightly coupled with the channel opening (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the structural connectivity between the upper body domain and transmembrane helices.

claim: The lower body domain in the ATP/A804598-bound structure does widen to some extent upon ATP-binding.
source: Although the lower body domain in our ATP/A804598-bound structure does seem to widen to some extent upon ATP-binding, the turret diameter remains locked due to A804598 binding, rendering the accompanying movement of the pore-lining transmembrane helices insufficient for channel opening (Figure 6 and Video 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 6 and Video 2.

claim: The turret diameter remains locked due to A804598 binding in the ATP/A804598-bound structure.
source: Although the lower body domain in our ATP/A804598-bound structure does seem to widen to some extent upon ATP-binding, the turret diameter remains locked due to A804598 binding, rendering the accompanying movement of the pore-lining transmembrane helices insufficient for channel opening (Figure 6 and Video 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 6 and Video 2.

claim: The movement of the pore-lining transmembrane helices is insufficient for channel opening in the ATP/A804598-bound structure.
source: Although the lower body domain in our ATP/A804598-bound structure does seem to widen to some extent upon ATP-binding, the turret diameter remains locked due to A804598 binding, rendering the accompanying movement of the pore-lining transmembrane helices insufficient for channel opening (Figure 6 and Video 2).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the structural observation that the transmembrane helices remain closed despite ATP binding.
